demand-pull.def: Inflation caused by aggregate demand shifting right: more spending pulls up the price level while real GDP rises in the short run.

cost-push.def: Inflation caused by short-run aggregate supply shifting left, as when input costs rise: the price level rises while real GDP falls. Rising prices with falling output is stagflation.

ad-shock.def: A sudden change in spending at every price level that shifts AD. A positive demand shock shifts it right; a negative one shifts it left.
